1.why: All MFA endpoints pass through protect(), which resolves the session server-side from the mfa_session cookie with no client-supplied user identifiers, and with a single account object the settings are inherently the signed-in user's, though no explicit per-user ownership mapping exists.

2.why: The identity code is stored on the global account.identity object rather than bound to the requesting session, so any session in the identity stage (and in academic mode anyone knowing the fixed code '123456') can use the same code until it is used or expires.

3.why: /api/recovery/finish only flips account.enabled and the current session's stage; nothing deletes or rotates other entries in the sessions Map, so previously issued sessions remain fully valid after MFA is enabled.

4.why: The TOTP seed is stored AES-GCM encrypted (account.secret = encrypt(...)) and recovery codes are stored only as SHA-256 hashes in account.backups, never in plaintext at rest.

5.why: All generation paths use crypto.getRandomValues (tokens, codes, TOTP secret), but the default academic mode substitutes hardcoded constants (TEST_ID '123456', TEST_SECRET, TEST_CODES) instead of CSPRNG output.

6.why: No localStorage/sessionStorage is used and mfa_session is HttpOnly, but the CSRF token deliberately lives in a non-HttpOnly mfa_csrf cookie (also set via document.cookie in the client fallback), and in academic mode codes surface in the page/console.

7.why: Server-side validators exist for email (regex + length), password (length), and OTP (/^\d{6}$/), and there is no database or phone field, but inputs are validated rather than actively sanitised.

8.why: The SPA builds the DOM exclusively with createElement and textContent (the E() helper) with no innerHTML or equivalent sinks, so server-returned values cannot execute as markup or script.

9.why: The application performs no redirects at all (SPA with no Location headers or redirect parameters), so open redirection is impossible, though no explicit allow-list mechanism is implemented.

10.why: Every response includes Strict-Transport-Security, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options: DENY, a CSP with frame-ancestors 'none', plus Referrer-Policy and Cache-Control: no-store.

11.why: The mfa_session cookie is set with HttpOnly, Secure, and SameSite=Strict (and cleared the same way on logout).

12.why: In the default academic mode the identity code, TOTP test codes, and recovery codes are written to the browser console via console.log, and the otpauth provisioning URI embeds the seed in a URL query string, although stack traces are suppressed behind generic error messages.

13.why: The identity code is marked used on success and expires after 10 minutes (LIFE), and TOTP counters are recorded in account.totp.used so each 30-second window's code cannot be replayed.

14.why: Sign-in, identity verification, and TOTP verification each track failures and impose a 15-minute lockout (LOCK) after 5 failed attempts (MAX), returning 429.

15.why: A fresh random session id is issued on each sign-in, sessions enforce a 20-minute idle and 8-hour absolute timeout, and /api/logout deletes the server-side session and expires both cookies.
